newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian Pacific sells real estate unit for C$952 million.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Pacific sells real estate unit for C$952 million.

text.p: Canadian Pacific Ltd. said Friday it will sell most of its Canadian real estate arm to Oxford Properties Group Inc. and a unit of General Electric Co. for C$952 million ($694 million).
Canadian Pacific, the country's largest conglomerate, said the sale price of the real estate portfolio includes the assumption of debt by the buyers.
The conglomerate is selling two of its wholly-owned real estate units, Marathon Realty Co. Ltd. and Centrixx Realty Holdings Ltd.
The units comprise about 12 million square feet of office and retail properties across Canada. They include properties in Toronto, Montreal, Ottawa, Calgary and Quebec City.

Canadian Pacific said it would sell the real estate portfolio to a newly incorporated company that will be owned equally by Oxford and General Electric Capital Corp. GE Capital is a wholly owned unit of Fairfield, Conn.-based General Electric Co.

The agreement does not include Canadian Pacific's U.S. retail assets, which are in the process of being sold to First Union Real Estate Investment Trust. The agreement also excludes Canadian Pacific's land and development sites.
Canadian Pacific said the sale of the real estate portfolio will allow it to focus resources on its core operations, which include transportation, energy and hotel businesses.

"For some time now it has been know that CP was looking to downsize the real estate operations," said Ted Larkin, a transportation analyst with Bunting Warburg Inc. "What this deal does today is take care of the dispensation of the Canadian properties in one fell swoop."

For Canadian Pacific the deal will take about C$800 million ($582 million) in debt off of the company's balance sheet, said Larkin. He said the sale announcement had little impact on the company's stock price because it had been widely anticipated.

Toronto-based Oxford said it would manage the properties being purchased and expects to employ most of the Marathon employees now overseeing the properties. GE Capital Canada Inc. would provide a first mortgage financing facility, the companies said.
"This acquisition will nearly double Oxford's asset base, and will extend the company's property management business to 45 million square fee," Oxford Chief Executive Jon Love said in a statement.

Oxford said it will borrow $100 million from Burcon International Developments Ltd. to complete the purchase. Burcon, Oxford's largest shareholder, has agreed to lend the money on market terms and conditions, Oxford said.
